coordinateConvention: Planetocentric latitude; east-positive longitude; interpreted in MOON_ME_DE440_ME421. Published rounded coordinates are not survey-grade.

sites.name: Odysseus · IM-1
sites.touchdownPrecision: to the minute; NASA reported 6:23 p.m. EST
sites.outcome: First U.S. soft landing since 1972. Odysseus came to rest tilted after touchdown and returned data for about a week.
sites.note: NASA reports a 12° local slope. A past touchdown does not certify a site for another lander.

sites.name: Athena · IM-2
sites.touchdownPrecision: approximate; NASA reported about 11:30 a.m. Central
sites.outcome: Landed on its side, so the PRIME-1 drill and mass spectrometer could not meet their goals; the mission ended within about a day.
sites.nasaPayloads: PRIME-1: TRIDENT drill and MSOLO mass spectrometer
sites.note: LRO located Athena inside a 20 m crater after it landed on its side. This terrain is unresolved in the regional DEM.

sites.name: Blue Ghost · Mission 1
sites.touchdownPrecision: to the minute; NASA reported 3:34 a.m. EST
sites.outcome: Landed upright and delivered all 10 NASA payloads, operating through a full lunar day.
sites.note: LROC imagery places the lander on a small crater rim. Compare its low-latitude daylight cycle with the southern sites.

sites.name: Apollo 11 · Tranquility
sites.crew: Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin; Michael Collins in lunar orbit
sites.outcome: First crewed landing, about 21.5 hours on the surface.
sites.coordinatePrecision: LRO-derived ME/PA DE421 coordinates; printed digits are not a survey error bound
sites.note: NASA NSSDCA lunar-module location. Historical hardware is not assumed operational at the selected date.

sites.name: Apollo 12 · Intrepid
sites.crew: Pete Conrad and Alan Bean; Richard Gordon in lunar orbit
sites.outcome: Pinpoint landing within walking distance of the Surveyor 3 probe, about 31.5 hours on the surface.
sites.coordinatePrecision: LRO-derived ME/PA DE421; 4 decimal places published
sites.note: An equatorial western-longitude comparison, using NASA's lunar-module coordinate table.

sites.name: Apollo 17 · Challenger
sites.crew: Eugene Cernan and Harrison Schmitt; Ronald Evans in lunar orbit
sites.outcome: Most recent crewed landing as of 2026, about 75 hours on the surface.
sites.coordinatePrecision: LRO-derived ME/PA DE421; 4 decimal places published
sites.note: A valley location for terrain comparisons; the global DEM does not resolve every local hazard.
